title: Armed men take 25 hostages at supermarket in one of Colombia’s top tourist destinations
summary:
Police say group seized store in city of Cartagena and local media showed footage of snipers on nearby buildings

A group of armed men with their faces covered seized a supermarket in the

blocks.text: A group of armed men with their faces covered seized a supermarket in the Colombian city of Cartagena on Tuesday and are holding 25 people hostage, the president, Abelardo de la Espriella, said on Tuesday.
De la Espriella, said the men were “common criminals” who fled into the supermarket after a failed attempt to hold up an armored truck.
Military and police forces have been deployed to the hostage site, Colombian police said.

Footage shared on social media showed dozens of people rushing out of the Exito supermarket in Cartagena’s La Castellana neighborhood, while local media have shown footage of snipers on nearby buildings in what appears to be a standoff between the armed men and police.

“Thirty people were kidnapped, five ​of whom have already been released. They are older women,” said de la Espriella from the city of ​Villavicencio, where he traveled after an overnight bombing ​there.

Cartagena is one of Colombia’s main tourist destinations. The city of a million people is famous for its well-preserved 18th-century architecture, and the thick stone walls built to defend it from pirate attacks.

The Rafael Núñez airport in Cartagena temporarily suspended its operations on Tuesday after the incident, as the armed forces used one of the runways in ​connection with ​the incident. It later said operations were slowly returning to normal and landings were reopened about 45 minutes after the suspension.
